evidence_summary: Herald is documented as a Chicago-based importer/brand using Japanese OEM production; the AM-44A is its identified dirt pedal. Related retail names include Apollo, LRE, Melos, Mica, Monacor and Olson, making this a high-value OEM reconciliation target.

Top Gear is associated with Hawkes Electronics / Len Hawkes and produced a rare UK dirt catalog. The Top Gear Fuzz is documented as closely related to the Fuzz Sustain and also appears in the Guild Grizzly relationship discussion.

Period evidence places the Fuzz Sustain in the mid/late 1970s; a 1975 UK trade advertisement lists it, and specialist research identifies it as a combined fuzz/treble-boost product. A three-knob state is documented, with a two-knob version linked to the Guild Grizzly Fuzz relationship.
German Karlsruhe builder founded by Gerard Daleiden. Zuzz Thainer is documented as a combination fuzz, sustainer and noise gate and is one of the builder's rare surviving products.

ToneHome preserves the model as a rare Lemon StudioSound product and provides period Fachblatt evidence. It is retained as a catalog boundary/product-family record while dirt relevance is being separated from the builder's wider effects catalog.
